core_obligations: Enumerate the approximations (proof lines 3283-3301): choose a set I of finitely presented modules with maps to F such that every finitely presented module mapping to F is isomorphic over F to one of them, and let the index category have these objects with morphisms those compatible with the maps to F.

Show the index category is filtered (proof lines 3303-3350): for two indices the direct sum of the two maps is again a finitely presented module mapping to F, so it is isomorphic to one of the enumerated ones and provides an upper bound; for a parallel pair of morphisms the cokernel of their difference is finitely presented and maps to F, and the corresponding index equalizes the pair, so the category is filtered.

Identify the colimit (proof lines 3352-3400): the canonical map from the colimit to F is checked on stalks; for injectivity a section mapping to zero is killed after replacing the index by the quotient of the kernel of its map by the finite type subsheaf generated by that section over a quasi-compact open, using the extension lemma; for surjectivity a section of F over a quasi-compact open extends to a finitely presented module mapping to F by the finitely presented extension lemma, and that map is isomorphic to one of the enumerated maps.
proof_roadmap: Enumerate the finitely presented modules mapping to the given module and organize them into a category.
Verify the filteredness conditions by taking direct sums for upper bounds and cokernels of differences for equalizers.
Check the canonical map to the module is an isomorphism on stalks, using the extension lemmas to kill sections and to produce sections.
difficulty_reason: The lemma proves that every quasi-coherent module on a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme is the filtered colimit of the finitely presented modules mapping to it, indexed by a filtered category (statement lines 3256-3281). The proof (proof lines 3283-3407) enumerates the finitely presented modules mapping to the given one, verifies the filteredness conditions through direct sums and cokernels of differences, and identifies the colimit with the module by checking injectivity and surjectivity on stalks with the help of the two extension lemmas. H3: an original filtered-category construction with a stalkwise identification, written out in full.
